newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's bishops blast Cardoso's economic policies.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's bishops blast Cardoso's economic policies.

text.p: Brazil's Catholic Bishops on Thursday launched a stinging attack against the free market policies of President Fernando Henrique Cardoso and called for the adoption of a new model for economic development.

In a statement released during the annual general assembly of the National Conference of Bishops of Brazil, the Church leaders said they could not accept the "neoliberal" policies adopted by the Cardoso administration.
"The impoverishment of the people cannot be accepted as the inevitable cost of economic development," the bishops said in the statement.

In a separate document the bishops also called for a suspension of the April 29 privatisation of state mining giant Vale de Rio Doce until Congress had been given more time to debate the implications of the sale.

"In light of serious ethical considerations we feel compelled in our role as pastors to express our concern before actions that will irrevocably and seriously affect the future of the country," the bishops said in the statement.
The bishops' criticism appeared timed to coincide with a massive opposition march against the Cardoso administration in the Brazilian capital on Thursday.

Thousands of landless peasants, industrial workers and members of opposition parties gathered in Brasilia to protest against the government's agrarian reform policies, its privatisation programme and rising unemployment.
In their statement, the bishops urged the government to reconsider its economic development model and called for the adoption of a far-reaching agrarian reform programme.
They said that considering Brazil had one of the world's worst income distributions, government policies should focus on eradicating illiteracy, fighting hunger and guaranteeing housing.
With over 100 million faithful, Brazil has the world's largest Catholic community and the Church is influential at all levels of society.
